title: "Pathaanon Se Kehna, Chauhaan Aa Raha Hai": Ajay Devgn Drops a Balaclava, a Bachchan Anthem, and a Not-So-Subtle Dig at Shah Rukh
excerpt: On his late father Veeru Devgan's birth anniversary, the OG action star announced 'Chauhaan' — a Kashmir-set mass actioner landing October 1, 2027 — and the internet immediately decided which Khan he was throwing shade at.
body:
The teaser opens on a riot. Stones fly, militants swarm army men in a grey Kashmir dawn, and the whole thing has the grim, washed-out palette of a film that wants you to feel the cold. And then — because this is **Ajay Devgn**, and subtlety has never been the point — a figure in a half-face balaclava walks in to the unmistakable thump of Amitabh Bachchan's *Jumma Chumma De De*. Two minutes and twenty-four seconds later, he plants himself in frame and growls the line that has been screenshotted, slowed down, and stitched into a thousand reels since: *"Pathaanon se kehna, Chauhaan aa raha hai."*

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=Czvourwg_30</youtube>

Tell the Pathaans: Chauhaan is coming.

If that sounds like a gauntlet thrown at a certain superstar's most famous franchise, well — the internet did the math in about four seconds flat. Whether or not Jio Studios intended a swipe at **Shah Rukh Khan**'s *Pathaan*, the line landed like one, and Bollywood Twitter has been gleefully refereeing the imaginary feud ever since. "The OG Boss has arrived," one fan declared. "Sure shot blockbuster loading," promised another. Subtle, this is not. Effective, it absolutely is.

**Chauhaan** was announced on June 25 — pointedly, on the birth anniversary of Devgn's late father, the legendary action director **Veeru Devgan**. That timing is the emotional spine of the whole rollout. This isn't just another star vehicle; it's a son building a temple to the kind of cinema his father spent a lifetime choreographing. "We are bringing back our OG action star in an action entertainer built for the big screen," the studio wrote, signing off with a line to Veeru Ji "for a legacy that continues to inspire generations." For an actor who came up watching his father stage stunts, the gesture reads as genuine rather than promotional.

> "Pathaanon se kehna, Chauhaan aa raha hai." — Ajay Devgn, in the announcement teaser

Here's what we know about the film itself, which is deliberately not much. It's a **Jio Studios** presentation, a **Colour Yellow** production — which means **Aanand L Rai** (the *Tanu Weds Manu* and *Raanjhanaa* man, an unexpectedly soft hand for a hard-edged actioner) is steering the ship, alongside writer **Himanshu Sharma** and director **Neeraj Yadav**. The setup is unambiguous: a Kashmir gripped by militancy, and a man positioned as the "permanent solution" to it. It is, in other words, squarely in the muscular nationalist-actioner lane that has minted money across Indian cinema for the better part of a decade — the *Uri*, *Pathaan*, *Fighter* corridor — and Devgn, with *Tanhaji* and *Singham* in his back pocket, has a better claim to that throne than almost anyone.

The casting and finer plot details remain under wraps, which is smart. Right now the entire pitch is mood: a balaclava, a Bachchan anthem repurposed as a war cry, and that one dialogue. The film doesn't arrive until **October 1, 2027** — a full fifteen months out — so this is pure flag-planting, a way to stake a Dussehra-season date and let the buzz marinate.

And it's worth noting how busy Devgn's slate already is. The long-awaited *Ranger*, his action-adventure opposite **Sanjay Dutt** and **Tamannaah Bhatia**, is eyeing a December 4, 2026 release, and *Dhamaal 4* just blinked and sprinted to July 10 to dodge Christopher Nolan's *The Odyssey*. The man is not slowing down at 57; he's accelerating.

For the diaspora, *Chauhaan* will almost certainly follow the now-standard playbook for a Devgn tentpole — a wide theatrical release across the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf through the usual distributors, dubbed Tamil and Telugu prints to chase the pan-India audience, and a streaming landing on a major platform a few weeks after its run. Expect Friday-night-in-Edison, packed-Cineworld-in-Wembley energy when it finally drops.

Fifteen months is a long time to keep a war cry warm. But if *Chauhaan* delivers even half the swagger of its announcement, that balaclava is going to sell a lot of tickets. The Pathaans, presumably, have been warned.
